CFML Language Reference: Functions

Find

Searches a string for a substring and returns the position where it first appears. The search is case-sensitive.

Category

String functions

Syntax

Find(substring, string [, start ])

Parameters

substring
The text to look for.
string
The string to search.
start
Optional. Position at which to start searching. Default 1.

Returns

The position (1 = first character) of the first occurrence, or 0 if the substring is not found or is empty.

Usage

The argument order trips up everyone at least once: the thing you are looking for comes first. Use FindNoCase for a case-insensitive search, FindOneOf to look for any one of several characters, and REFind to search with a regular expression.

To find every occurrence, call Find in a loop, starting each search one character after the last hit.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Text = "To be or not to be, that is the question">
<CFSET Pos = Find("be", Text)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<P><I>#Text#</I></P>
<UL>
<LI>Find("be", Text) = #Pos#
<LI>Next "be" after that: #Find("be", Text, Pos + 1)#
<LI>Find("To", Text) = #Find("To", Text)#, but Find("TO", Text) = #Find("TO", Text)#
<LI>Find("Hamlet", Text) = #Find("Hamlet", Text)#
</UL>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

FindNoCase, FindOneOf, REFind, Replace, ListFind
